complexity.reason: Dominant term n^2: 2 nested loops over items; sequential loops are additive, the largest wins.
assumptions: n = number of elements in items
Hash-based Map/Set operations are treated as O(1) on average.
Constructor of Item only stores its arguments into fields, so it is O(1).
String/StringBuilder operations are treated as O(1) (short strings).
List.get/set/add are treated as O(1), assuming a random-access list such as ArrayList.
limitations: Static upper-bound estimate from the source; no execution, no profiling.
Loop bounds come from recognised counter, collection-size and midpoint-search patterns; anything else is unknown.
A callee is trusted only when it is proven O(1); a callee's cost as a function of its arguments is not tracked.
Standard-library costs assume typical implementations (see assumptions); user-defined generics and streams are unknown.

finding.explanation: The loop over 'items' on line 521 searches for a matching element, and it runs once per iteration of the enclosing loop. Each search is O(n), so the nested work grows as O(n*m) (O(n^2) when both loops cover the same data).
finding.message: Repeated linear scan of 'items' inside a loop
finding.recommendation: The inner loop does not stop at the first match, so index 'items' as a Map<Key, List<Element>> (group by the compared value) built once before the outer loop. Assumes keys have consistent equals()/hashCode() and 'items' is not modified meanwhile.

finding.explanation: Strings are immutable: every concatenation on line 632 copies all characters collected so far, so building the result takes up to quadratic time in its length.
finding.message: String 'labels' is extended inside a loop
finding.recommendation: Collect the pieces in a StringBuilder and call toString() once after the loop (or use String.join / Collectors.joining).
